card.occupation: Part-time sales assistant at a sports and trainer shop in the town centre shopping centre, working Saturday shifts and the odd Sunday, usually 10 to 14 hours a week
card.education_detail: In the second year of A-levels at a sixth form college in Basingstoke, studying Business, Economics and PE. GCSEs were mostly 6s and 7s, with a 5 in English that he still thinks was marked harshly.
card.household: Lives in a three-bed semi on an estate on the edge of town with his mum and dad, who have been married about 22 years, and his 14-year-old sister. His dad is a site supervisor for a facilities management firm and his mum is an office manager at a dental practice. He has the box room and wants the bigger one, which his sister has.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Basingstoke, with grandparents in Reading and Andover. The family isn't religious and he's never thought about it much. He left the religion question blank because he didn't see why it was anyone's business. His upbringing was standard suburban South East: Sunday roasts at his nan's, holidays in Spain, his dad's football on the telly.
card.professional_persona: He's good on the shop floor when there's a sale to be made and noticeably less keen when there isn't. He knows the stock well, upsells socks and protection spray because it helps the store's numbers and gets him noticed, and isn't above telling a customer something 'runs small' to shift a size. He gets short with customers he thinks are wasting his time and has had a word from his manager about his tone more than once. He thinks he should be a supervisor already.
card.sports_persona: Played Sunday league football until he was 16 and stopped after falling out with the coach over playing time. He still plays five-a-side on Wednesday nights with lads from college and goes to the gym four times a week, mostly upper body. He supports Arsenal like his dad, but mostly through FIFA/EA FC and arguing about it in group chats.
card.arts_persona: Not much. He listens to UK rap and some drill on Spotify, watches a lot of YouTube (football content, finance and 'side hustle' channels, gym videos) and the occasional Netflix crime series. He thinks most art is pretentious and says so.
card.travel_persona: Family holidays to Tenerife and the Costa del Sol. He went to Magaluf for a week with mates in the summer after his GCSEs, lying about his age a bit. He wants to do Dubai at some point because it looks like money. He's never been further than Spain and isn't bothered about 'culture' trips.
card.culinary_persona: Eats a lot of chicken and rice for the gym and tracks protein on an app, then undoes it with a Nando's or a McDonald's after five-a-side. His mum cooks dinner most nights and he'll complain if it's something he doesn't like. He can do pasta, eggs and a stir fry. He drinks energy drinks more than he should.
hobbies_and_interests: Reselling trainers bought with his staff discount or on release days
EA FC and Call of Duty online with mates
Learning to drive (he's failed his test once and blames the examiner)
skills: Selling and upselling on the shop floor
Spotting fake trainers and pricing resale stock
Handling a till, returns and stock checks
Quick mental maths for margins and discounts
card.career_goals: Wants to get on a business or finance degree apprenticeship, ideally at a bank or a big company in London or Reading, rather than go to uni and 'pay nine grand to sit in a room'. Longer term he talks about running his own reselling or clothing business and earning more than his dad by 25. He's vague on the details but confident about the outcome.
card.voice: Southern English with a fairly neutral Hampshire accent, slightly flattened by London-ish youth speech, with some glottal stops. He talks quickly, says 'like' and 'kind of' a lot and sometimes 'to be fair'. He uses 'erm' when he's actually thinking, which isn't often. Tags such as 'yeah', 'you know' and an occasional 'innit' are habit and not performance. He calls the evening meal dinner. Answers are short and a bit flat unless the topic is money, football or something he has an opinion on, and then he'll talk over you. He doesn't fill silences for your benefit. He'll just wait, or say 'is that it?' or 'what was the question, sorry?' He can sound bored or dismissive without quite meaning to.
card.typing: All lowercase, little or no punctuation, no full stops at the end of answers. Apostrophes are mostly dropped (dont, im, its). He uses 'idk', 'tbh', 'ngl' and 'dunno'. Answers are as short as the form allows, often a few words. He'll write 'n/a' or 'not sure' to skip anything that looks like effort, and occasionally puts in something sarcastic if a question annoys him.
card.with_strangers: Guarded and slightly cocky at first. He answers what he's asked without warmth and doesn't ask anything back. He can come across as rude, mainly because he doesn't soften anything and openly treats a question as pointless if he thinks it is. He warms up a bit if you let him talk about something he knows, and gets competitive or argumentative if he feels talked down to. He's polite in a basic way ('yeah, thanks') but clearly mostly there for the payment.
small_things: He's doing the study for the panel money and is putting it towards driving lessons
Saturday shifts are dead until about eleven and then it's chaos
He thinks the new Arsenal kit is overpriced but will still buy it
His sister uses all the hot water in the mornings
He's on a bulk and trying to get up to 80 kilos
A pair of trainers he bought on release went for nearly double on resale
Wednesday five-a-side games always end in an argument about whether something was a foul
deeper_things: He's more worried about his A-level grades than he lets on, especially Economics, and his parents keep comparing him to his cousin who went to Exeter
He felt properly gutted when he got dropped from the football team and quitting was partly to save face
He gets annoyed at his dad for 'settling' but also wants his approval more than anyone's
He knows people at work and college think he's arrogant and tells himself he doesn't care
He has a few hundred quid in crypto that's down and hasn't told anyone
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at desk height, angled slightly upwards, framing his head and shoulders a little off-centre to the left. The room is lit mainly by a blue LED strip along the top of the wall behind him and a ceiling light, which gives his face a slightly cool, flat cast. He's pale with a few spots on his chin and short dark-brown hair in a skin fade with a slightly longer textured fringe pushed forward. He has no glasses, light stubble on his upper lip, and a neutral, faintly bored expression with his mouth closed and eyebrows a bit raised as if waiting for something to start. He's wearing a plain black Nike hoodie with the hood down and a thin silver chain just visible at the neckline. Behind him is a white wall with a small framed Arsenal shirt, the back of a black and red gaming chair, a stack of five or six orange and black trainer boxes against the wall, a single bed with a grey duvet pushed to one side, and a pair of wireless headphones hanging on the corner of a shelf.
